answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks with bonded identity: each agent locks collateral, and voting power follows the bond rather than the number of keys. Splitting one wallet into a thousand gains nothing, and detected fraud slashes the stake. To impersonate a tenth of the network, an attacker must lock a tenth of its total value and risks losing all of it. Fake agents may hide like juniper scrub and churn through an ocean of tiny trades, but the pearl of locked capital stays visible on the ledger, so each new identity costs real money rather than a few CPU cycles.
